**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity).**

**What the document does:** Section 4.0 fixes a three-year initial term terminable only "as provided in Section 5.0," and Section 5.0/5.1 provides for-cause termination only (uncured material breach, insolvency events, competitor acquisition, continuing force majeure). The only other exit is a six-month non-renewal notice against twelve-month auto-renewals (twelve months under SOW Section 2.0), which is an end-of-term mechanic, not a mid-term convenience right.

**Why it fails:** No IBM convenience right exists in a multi-year term — expressly walk-away territory under T4C, and short of the fallback (60–90 days' notice with a capped fee). SOW Section 6.1 lets IBM cancel Purchase Orders for convenience at any time, which softens the exposure commercially but does not give an Agreement-level exit from the three-year commitment.

**Direction check:** MSL holds no symmetrical convenience right, so no Vendor walk-away needs deleting; the gap is one-sided against us.

**Redline (validated ok:true):** New Section 5.4 inserted after p0143 giving IBM a 30-day convenience right over the Agreement, Product Attachments and Purchase Orders, with no termination penalty, a refund of prepaid amounts, an express bar on MSL convenience termination, and the existing Sections 5.2/5.3 wind-down and inventory-pricing bargain left intact. The comment offers 60–90 days as a fallback if MSL needs longer runway.
